$comment: Meta's leadgen webhook, read from its Webhooks-for-Leadgen reference and its general webhook signing docs. This is the FIRST provider to exercise verification.header.format `prefixed` -- Stripe uses `compound`, and until now `prefixed` and `raw` were declared in the vocabulary and driven by nothing, which is the shape this repo keeps finding: a declaration that silently does nothing.
title: Facebook lead
description: Start when somebody submits a Facebook lead form. The delivery carries only IDS -- pair this with the `lead_get` action to read the answers.
setup: In the Meta app dashboard, add a Webhooks product, subscribe to the PAGE object and tick the `leadgen` field, and point the callback URL at the route your host mounts for this trigger. Meta first sends a GET carrying `hub.mode=subscribe`, `hub.verify_token` and `hub.challenge` -- the host must echo `hub.challenge` back as the body and check `hub.verify_token` against the value set in the dashboard, or the subscription is never activated. Then subscribe the app to each Page (`POST /{pageId}/subscribed_apps` with `subscribed_fields=leadgen`), which is a SEPARATE step: a webhook configured but not subscribed per Page delivers nothing and reports nothing.

verification.$payloadComment: The RAW bytes as received. Re-serialised JSON changes key order and whitespace and produces a mismatch indistinguishable from a wrong secret -- and Meta escapes non-ASCII in its payloads, so a body that round-trips through a parser comes back with different bytes for any lead whose name is not ASCII. That is a failure that only appears for some people's names.

header.$comment: Quoting Meta: the signature is included in the X-Hub-Signature-256 header 'preceded with sha256='. A comparison that forgets to strip the prefix never matches; one that strips it with a fixed offset breaks if Meta ever sends the older X-Hub-Signature (sha1=), which is seven characters rather than eight.

verification.$secretComment: The APP SECRET, not a per-endpoint signing secret. Stripe mints one secret per endpoint so a leaked one exposes one endpoint; Meta signs every webhook for the app with the one value that also keys appsecret_proof. That is a real difference in blast radius and it is the provider's, not ours -- but it means rotating the app secret invalidates outgoing proofs and incoming signatures at the same instant, and a host that updates one credential field will have broken the other.
verification.$timestampComment: There is NO timestamp and therefore no tolerance. Meta sends none, so a captured delivery stays valid forever and replay protection cannot come from the signature -- it has to come from de-duplicating on leadgen_id. Stated here rather than left as an absence, because `tolerance` being missing looks like an oversight and is not.

config.label: Form IDs
config.description: Comma separated. Leave blank to accept every form on every subscribed Page. A delivery whose form_id is not listed settles the trigger without starting the graph.

outputShape.description: The lead's id, and the ONLY way to reach the answers -- pass it to `lead_get`. Meta redelivers on failure, and there is no timestamp in the signature, so dedupe on this.
The Page the form belongs to.
Which lead form was submitted. Branch on this when one Page runs several.
The ad that produced the lead. Absent for an organic form submission.
The ad set. Meta still calls it adgroup on this payload.
Unix seconds. When the person submitted, not when the delivery arrived.
